hints: Focus on what percentage by mass really means, mass of carbon divided by total Mr, times 100.
Try calculating it for a hexose, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$ has a carbon mass of $6 \times 12 = 72$ out of an Mr of 180.
Now do the same quick check for a pentose, starch monomer and sucrose, and look for the pair where both give exactly 40%.
walkthrough:
**Recall the percentage by mass rule**

Great start, this is just a composition calculation. For any compound, the % of carbon is the total mass of carbon atoms divided by the total Mr.

$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{\text{mass of C atoms}}{M_r} \times 100$$

**Check the monosaccharides**

For a pentose, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5$:
$$M_r = (5 \times 12) + (10 \times 1) + (5 \times 16) = 60 + 10 + 80 = 150$$
$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{60}{150} \times 100 = 40\%$$
For a hexose, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$:
$$M_r = (6 \times 12) + (12 \times 1) + (6 \times 16) = 72 + 12 + 96 = 180$$
$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{72}{180} \times 100 = 40\%$$
So both of these fit the 40% condition perfectly.

**Check starch and sucrose**

For starch monomer, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5$:
$$M_r = 72 + 10 + 80 = 162$$
$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{72}{162} \times 100 = 44.4\%$$
For sucrose, $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$:
$$M_r = 144 + 22 + 176 = 342$$
$$\% \text{ C} = \frac{144}{342} \times 100 = 42.1\%$$
Neither of these is 40%. Only the pentose plus hexose pair works.

options.A: Hexose is correct at 40% carbon, but starch is about 44.4% carbon because it has lost water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) during condensation. Since K does not fit, this pair is wrong.
options.B: Both are correct. Pentose gives 60/150 x 100 = 40% and hexose gives 72/180 x 100 = 40%. This is the only pair where J and K both contain 40% carbon by mass.
options.C: Pentose is correct at 40%, but sucrose is about 42.1% carbon (144/342 x 100). Students often assume all carbohydrates have the same %C, but the disaccharide has a different C:H:O ratio after condensation.
options.D: Neither fits. Starch is about 44.4% and sucrose is about 42.1%. Both are condensation products with less oxygen and hydrogen per carbon, so their %C is higher than 40%.
